title: How many angles of symmetry does a square have?
description: A square is turned about its centre. It overlaps itself after each quarter turn, and a full turn brings every corner back to its own place, giving four angles of symmetry. Keeko's doubt is that the full turn does not count, so there are only three.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square matches itself after ninety, one hundred and eighty, two hundred and seventy and three hundred and sixty degrees, and the full turn counts too. Watch for students who leave out the full turn.

source: How many angles of symmetry does a square have? How much rot
video_script.why: The child turns a square quarter by quarter, finds the four turns after which it overlaps itself, and sees that the full turn counts as the fourth.
video_script.substitution: Turn the square about its centre in steps of a quarter turn and note each turn after which it overlaps itself.
video_script.anchor: a square with a small dot at each corner and a red dot at its centre
video_script.wrong_answer: the full turn does not count, so there are only three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the full turn does not count, so there are only three. At the full turn the square overlaps itself exactly, with every corner back in its own place, so it counts as the fourth angle of symmetry.
video_script.payoff_line: The square has four angles of symmetry

final_answer.value: 4 angles of symmetry: 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees; the square is back at its start after 360 degrees
final_answer.spoken: the square has four angles of symmetry

maths_rules: A turn about the centre after which a shape looks exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry
A square overlaps itself after each quarter turn: 90, 180 and 270 degrees
A full turn of 360 degrees brings every corner back to its own place, so it counts as the fourth angle of symmetry
A square has 4 angles of symmetry: 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees
In a 90 degree turn the corners move top left to top right, top right to bottom right, bottom right to bottom left, bottom left to top left
video_script.design: One idea: a square matches itself after every quarter turn, and the full turn is the fourth. The square stays on the board all video. Corners are named by position, never by letter. Wrong idea: the full turn does not count.
